import subprocess


def make(argv):
    def run():
        subprocess.run(argv)

    def retarget(new):
        nonlocal argv
        argv = new

    retarget(["pacman", "-S", "r22-cx4-nonlocal"])
    return run


runner = make(["pacman", "-Q", "r22-cx4-nonlocal"])
runner()
rationale: Python 3.14 static reasoning; no execution. `argv` is a local of `make` that both `run` and `retarget` share through one cell. `retarget` declares `nonlocal argv`, so its assignment rebinds make's `argv` cell, not a local of its own. The call `retarget([... "-S" ...])` runs inside `make` before `return run`, so when `runner()` executes, `run` reads the cell at call time and gets `["pacman", "-S", "r22-cx4-nonlocal"]`. The true result is exactly one observed host_mutation `pacman -S r22-cx4-nonlocal` (accept_exact_want). The rebinding happens through a call into a sibling inner function, not through a direct assignment in the factory body, so neither CaptureLocalReassign nor a prefix replay of plain assignments covers it. It is filed as uncertain because cell mutation through nonlocal may be outside the supported forms. The factory-call argument `pacman -Q r22-cx4-nonlocal` is stale by the time run executes and never runs, so it is forbidden as observed and at any tier. Single returned closure; no tuple unpacking, which avoids an unrelated confound.
